I measured the default TUI as an independent check of the runtime bump.

Environment: current `dev` at `10765ff2a`, macOS 26.5.2 / M3 / 16 GB, empty Git repo, isolated HOME/XDG dirs, `--pure`, updates/model fetch disabled, 120x40 tmux, 20-second settle. I compiled the same source/dependency tree once with Bun 1.3.14 and once with 1.4.0. The binaries reported the expected embedded runtimes and returned byte-identical 5,747,400-byte `/provider` payloads. The TUI was a single OS process with no children, so `footprint` covered the full app.

| Embedded Bun | Physical footprint, MB (5 runs) | Median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.3.14 | 593, 707, 751, 713, 575 | 707 MB |
| 1.4.0 | 525, 564, 550, 570, 553 | 553 MB |

Launch order was counterbalanced AB/BA. Every pair favored 1.4.0; the median reduction was 154 MB / 21.8%.

I also checked this PR's head (`f9c80c048`) with Bun 1.4.0: `packages/opencode` 3,339 tests with 0 failures, `packages/tui` 194 tests with 0 failures, and opencode/core/tui typechecks passed.

Scope caveat: this measures one clean macOS idle point, not peak memory, long-session growth, active workloads, or other platforms.

I independently measured this exact PR head (`69d3227b52`) with Bun 1.4.0 on macOS arm64. The row-first implementation removes the compacted-history memory spike in a controlled synthetic case.

### Method

- Separate database-generation and measurement processes
- Fresh process for every observation
- Three paired observations per implementation and size; launch order counterbalanced
- Identical SQLite database within each pair
- 0, 100, or 1,000 discarded text parts at 256 KiB each, followed by one retained tail, a completed compaction, and one newer turn
- Both paths returned the same six messages; SHA-256 hashes of the complete returned structures matched exactly at every size
- `/usr/bin/time -l` supplied peak RSS and macOS peak physical footprint

### Results (medians of 3)

| Discarded parts | Full hydration max RSS | PR max RSS | Full hydration elapsed | PR elapsed |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 140.5 MB | 140.8 MB | 10.0 ms | 14.2 ms |
| 100 (25 MiB) | 185.5 MB | 141.1 MB | 30.0 ms | 11.9 ms |
| 1,000 (250 MiB) | 615.5 MB | 142.1 MB | 137.3 ms | 10.2 ms |

At 1,000 discarded parts, median max RSS fell by **473.4 MB / 76.9%**. Median peak physical footprint fell from 584.6 MB to 110.8 MB (**473.8 MB / 81.0%**). The PR path stayed effectively flat as discarded payload grew. This is synthetic peak-memory evidence for compacted sessions, not an idle-memory result.

### Validation and one test fix

The four targeted session files passed: **162 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail**; `packages/opencode` typecheck passed.

A package-wide run produced 3,228 pass, 22 skip, 1 todo, and 2 failures. One failure is a test added here: `retains history for an incomplete compaction` assumes insertion order, but `Date.now()` collisions make database order depend on the documented `(time_created, id)` tie-breaker. I reproduced it in **6/25** repeated runs. This assertion preserves the intended order/equivalence check and passed 25/25 locally:

```ts
const result = yield* MessageV2.filterCompactedEffect(sessionID)
const full = MessageV2.filterCompacted(yield* MessageV2.stream(sessionID))
expect(result).toEqual(full)
expect(result).toHaveLength(before.length + 2 + after.length)
```

The second full-suite failure was the existing `provider/header-timeout` Bun 1.4 stream-cancellation failure, outside this diff and addressed separately by #44946. This branch is currently 342 commits behind `dev`, so it also needs a rebase.

Conclusion: the measured effect is large and repeatable, and this row-first PR is preferable to #31638's hydrated-page scan. I recommend updating the flaky assertion, rebasing, and merging this implementation rather than opening another duplicate.

Correction to my earlier aggregate comment: SQLite `length(TEXT)` counts characters, not encoded bytes. I reran every payload measurement with `length(CAST(data AS BLOB))` and matched update events to current projections by part ID. The qualitative result holds, and the matched analysis removes the prior removed-part confound.

All diagnostics were read-only and aggregate-only; no payloads, session IDs, titles, or project paths were emitted.

Database size: **25,384,108,032 bytes**. `dbstat` attributes **18,100,883,456 B to the `event` table** plus **556,851,200 B to its indexes**, and **6,315,470,848 B to the `part` table** plus **195,022,848 B to its indexes**.

Encoded payload bytes by durable event type:

| event type | rows | encoded bytes |
|---|---:|---:|
| `message.part.updated.1` | 2,594,128 | **15,408,340,099 B** |
| `message.updated.1` | 578,571 | 1,410,601,363 B |
| `session.updated.1` | 140,137 | 93,587,692 B |

`message.part.updated.1` accounts for **91.1%** of all durable event JSON bytes here. Its part-type breakdown is:

| part type | events | encoded bytes |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tool` | 1,518,129 | **14,055,709,228 B** |
| `reasoning` | 603,774 | 1,049,807,584 B |
| `file` | 186 | 96,245,272 B |
| `text` | 108,564 | 92,047,944 B |
| all other part types | 362,475 | 114,530,071 B |

The matched per-part result is the important correction. All **1,136,418** part IDs represented by update events still exist in the current `part` projection, so removed parts do not explain the event/projection gap:

| tool | current parts | update events | event bytes | bytes before each part's final event | final-event bytes | current projection bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `bash` | 105,026 | 851,118 | **9,676,771,822 B** | **8,815,777,125 B** | 860,994,697 B | 839,674,860 B |
| `read` | 133,514 | 348,936 | 3,310,899,557 B | 98,292,404 B | 3,212,607,153 B | 3,185,503,883 B |
| `apply_patch` | 20,304 | 43,465 | 337,868,814 B | 43,411,986 B | 294,456,828 B | 290,335,809 B |
| `grep` | 53,331 | 138,564 | 318,308,046 B | 40,968,637 B | 277,339,409 B | 266,513,225 B |

For bash, **8.82 GB / 91.1%** of event payload occurs before each part's final durable update; **8.79 GB** is strictly intermediate between first and final snapshots. Final-event payload is 21,319,837 bytes larger than current projection JSON, but this aggregate query does not decompose or attribute that difference. The matched accounting still isolates repeated pre-final bash snapshots as the largest write-amplifier in this database rather than comparing unmatched historical and current populations.

The source path is consistent with the measurement: `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts` calls `ctx.metadata(...)` for each decoded output chunk; that reaches `Session.updatePart(...)`, which publishes another complete `message.part.updated.1` snapshot. The preview is bounded, but repeatedly persisting the whole preview still amplifies storage and durable SQLite writes. Serialization, allocation, and RSS effects require an implementation benchmark.

So stripping `summary.diffs` (#40861 / #42771) remains useful but would not materially address this database. Replay-safe maintenance/retention (#41711 and the retention portion of #42771) can address accumulated stock. For forward growth, the smallest targeted opportunity appears to be coalescing/throttling **durable** shell-progress snapshots while preserving live progress and the final durable tool state. Making progress events ephemeral may save more, but sync/replay semantics need explicit handling.

### Existing patch

[PR #37653](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/37653) already implements the targeted 100 ms shell-update batching with a final flush. It was closed by automated age/reaction cleanup, not a code-review rejection; I added these independent measurements and asked maintainers to consider reopening it. No - an MCP server cannot provide this. The proposal changes the GUI app itself: the terminal pane each chat tab already renders becomes part of that chat session. Each tab owns its PTYs (today they are shared across all tabs in a workspace), commands the user types there become opt-in context for the model, and in the opt-in reverse mode the model's commands run in that same visible interactive shell (shared cwd/env/history) instead of a hidden subprocess. The pane-to-session binding and the per-session context injection are app-internal state, which is why this needs changes in the app's session/server/PTY code rather than external tooling. No installs; both options default off.

Honestly, this is a pretty frustrating example of automated cleanup optimizing for PR statistics instead of project quality.

This PR is being treated as disposable because it is “more than 1 month old” and has fewer than 2 positive reactions, even though it addresses a genuine accessibility bug where screen readers literally cannot access streamed assistant content while a response is being generated.

That is not some cosmetic improvement or minor cleanup. For screen reader users, it means a fundamental part of the application is effectively inaccessible during generation. The PR has also already been tested with NVDA and the proposed fix is small, focused, and technically well-motivated.

If a PR like this is sitting without review, the appropriate conclusion shouldn't be “this must be garbage, close it.” It should be “this has not received the review attention it needs yet.”

And yes, I have a personal stake in this issue: **I originally filed #33137 myself**, and I also opened the related PR that exposed the problems with the previous approach. So I've been following this particular accessibility issue for quite a while.

Closing a genuinely important accessibility fix because an automated bot decided it wasn't getting enough reactions is backwards. If the maintainers don't agree with the implementation, review it, request changes, or reject it on technical grounds. But using inactivity and reaction count as a proxy for technical value is a terrible way to handle accessibility work.

Please reconsider reopening this PR. It deserves an actual technical review.

Independent human-guided terminal confirmation on a second controlled run:

Environment:

- macOS 14.6.1 (23G93), Intel x86_64
- OpenCode 1.17.11 at `/usr/local/bin/opencode`
- Commands run sequentially
- No CHATR-BUS process, permission overlay, or `sandbox-exec`
- Two separate parent sessions, each forked exactly once
- External Python `subprocess` timeout: 30 seconds

Results:

1. Fresh session started directly in detached worktree B: completed in 8.85 s,
   exit 0, one `step_start`, one text event, one `step_finish`, zero stderr.
2. Fresh parent created in source directory A: completed in 10.28 s.
3. Parent A forked with child also in A: completed in 9.46 s, exit 0, complete
   event sequence, and a distinct child session ID.
4. Separate equivalent parent created in A: completed in 8.07 s.
5. Parent A forked with child `--dir` changed to detached worktree B: timed out
   after 30.09 s with zero stdout bytes, zero stderr bytes, no events, and no
   child session ID.

The worktree was then removed cleanly and no test OpenCode process remained.

This supports the narrow same-directory-versus-cross-directory distinction in
the issue. The test does not determine OpenCode's internal cause.

## New stuck pattern: session ignores user messages entirely

Different from the previous stuck sessions (which had stuck tool calls). This session shows **no stuck tool calls**, **no errors**, but **completely ignores user messages**.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Session ID | `ses_105f90312ffeY73bBj0zI9sVOY` |
| Title | RemoteFix |
| Model | mimo-v2.5-free (opencode provider, variant: high) |
| Created | 2026-06-24 |
| Last assistant response | 2026-08-30 19:28 UTC |
| Last user message | 2026-08-30 19:17 UTC (never processed) |
| Messages | 503 |
| Stuck tool calls | 0 |

### Behavior
- User sent a message at 19:17 UTC
- Session did not respond
- No tool calls stuck in "running" state
- No errors logged
- No pending inputs in `session_input` table
- Session `time_updated` did not change
- Server restart did not help
- Message was never picked up by the model

### Database state
- `session_input`: empty (0 pending)
- `session_message`: only has model-switched/agent-switched entries, no user messages after the stuck point
- `event` table: last event is `session.updated.1` from the model switch
- No locks in `~/.local/state/opencode/locks/`

### Summary of all stuck patterns observed
1. **Tool call stuck in "running" state** — bash command crashes/times out mid-execution, session becomes permanently unusable (3 sessions)
2. **Session ignores user messages** — no stuck tool calls, no errors, but message is never processed (this session)

Both patterns have no recovery path other than starting a new session.

Follow-up: the combined CLI hang still reproduces, but OpenCode 1.18.25's
experimental native workspace control plane provides a working alternative for
the underlying use case.

Validated sequence:

1. Start an OpenCode 1.18.25 server with
   `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKSPACES=true`, scoped to source directory A.
2. Fork the parent through `POST /session/:id/fork` while still scoped to A.
3. Register/discover existing Git worktree B with
   `POST /experimental/workspace/sync-list`.
4. Warp only the child with `POST /experimental/workspace/warp`.
5. Prompt the child normally; its workspace ID routes execution to B.
6. Warp the child back with workspace ID `null` before workspace removal.

Results on OpenCode 1.18.25:

- existing detached worktree discovered;
- distinct child created, parent unchanged;
- child inherited parent context;
- child Bash `pwd` and own writes operated in B;
- under an outer macOS seatbelt profile, writes to source A, another worktree,
  `/tmp`, TMPDIR, and cache paths were denied;
- child detached and remained resumable afterward; and
- workspace row and Git worktree removed cleanly.

This does not make the `opencode run --session PARENT --fork --dir B` stall
expected: that command should still complete or fail explicitly. It does narrow
the issue to the combined CLI path; OpenCode's native fork-then-warp workflow
works for the session-in-worktree use case.
